### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 967822acb6b82644170cf6bcbe580de871a44e8f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `40eac95f1b0a6f3cf326f0012a7ce4ce50bd72bf` — the merge of head `5c03334919c0bd69b4a65d537ac5c639f2972b7a` into base `967822acb6b82644170cf6bcbe580de871a44e8f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 40eac95f1b0a6f3cf326f0012a7ce4ce50bd72bf && git checkout 40eac95f1b0a6f3cf326f0012a7ce4ce50bd72bf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 967822acb6b82644170cf6bcbe580de871a44e8f 5c03334919c0bd69b4a65d537ac5c639f2972b7a && git checkout -B drift-repro 967822acb6b82644170cf6bcbe580de871a44e8f && git merge --no-ff 5c03334919c0bd69b4a65d537ac5c639f2972b7a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 967822acb6b82644170cf6bcbe580de871a44e8f
```

</details>

### ① Derived judgments

- **The one hunk.** `organizationAdminFailure`, grant leg: `organizationBoundaryFailure(setName, storedPermissionSetScope(column))` and nothing after it. The removed leg ran only for `t.next && column !== undefined`, and an organization administrator holds only insert and delete, so it ran only on an insert whose column is a non-blank string. Right.
- **What is judged is what the row confers.** The gate and the grant reader (`resolve-authz-context.ts`, lines 1509, 1585, 2667) both resolve `(name, column)` through `storedPermissionSetScope` and the one `resolvePermissionScoped`. The gate trims the column; the seam stores the trimmed value (`data[column] = chosen`). So the verdict is taken on the set the stored row resolves to, whether or not the seam judged the write (unsealed registry, undeclared column, unheld name). Right — the gate does not depend on the seam's refusal.
- **A named non-holder is refused when it must be.** The column names no servable holder ⇒ the resolver's stale arm reads it as no package ⇒ the bare-name answer: two holders refused naming both; one holder judged as that holder. Identical FROM and TO, because FROM's two legs gave the same answer there. Right.
- **The moved set, derived.** A cell moves only where the named leg passes and the bare leg failed: the column names a servable holder whose set is inside the boundary, and the bare name does not resolve to that same set. In the real registry that is two or more package holders only: a package-less row over a held name is a customization, never an environment item (`getEnvironmentScopedItem`); `permission` has no overridable baseline (`OVERRIDABLE_BASELINE_PACKAGES`); the catalog passes no `platformItem`; a disabled named holder is not servable and falls to the bare name, whose holder set still counts it. So the declared cell (two holders, in-boundary holder named: 403 → admit) is the only move. Right.
- **No environment answers differently today.** The registry refuses a second holder of a permission set (`registry.ts` 2862). Right.
- **Unchanged, by the diff:** system writes (short-circuit before this leg), removals, positions, the scoped-delegate leg `directGrantSet`, the denylist, the organization and membership checks. Right.

Measured on this head: `delegated-admin-gate.test.ts` 202/202; `@objectstack/plugin-security` suite 262 files, 6491 passed, 45 skipped (the dev's numbers). Ablation (gate file reverted to `main`, pins kept): exactly 2 red, the in-boundary-named pin in both administrator variants, with the bare-name message; restored, green. Probes, both variants, all as predicted: one outside holder with a non-holder named → refused (a); column as number, object, array, blank, null, boolean, wrong case, `pkg:name`, `__proto__`, `sys_metadata`, NUL-suffixed → refused naming both; padded in-boundary holder → admitted; a batch of one in and one out → refused; update → refused; another organization's row → refused; denylisted name with a package → refused by name; one inside holder with a non-holder named → admitted by the gate (the seam's 409, as before).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` — a fix lifting an over-refusal, no API or schema change. Right. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is on the changeset and the PR body, with the FROM → TO; `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. The widening is the one cell above and is pinned.

- Dev report 6822788987: `open_questions` empty, `security_findings: none`, `deviations` none. Agreed.
- Out-of-scope 1 (the sentence "which the position cannot resolve" on a direct grant): agreed, wording, follow-up.
- Out-of-scope 2 (`directGrantSet` still computes `restamped` under the pre-#32164 comment): agreed it is outside this card. By reading, it can only over-refuse and not for two package holders; follow-up card.
- Epic red lines: resolution not loosened (same resolver, same refusal); ambiguity reported, never guessed (no package and a non-holder still refuse naming both); independently releasable (no environment moves today); the moved answer declared and pinned. Held.
- Card acceptance: named package ⇒ that holder only ✔; comment matches the seam ✔; pins (in-boundary admitted, outside refused, none named refused, one-holder CONTROL) ✔; `Clause-②:` measured ✔.

### ④ Design judgment

`delegated-admin-gate.ts` — holds. No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits and follow-ups (none blocks; a separate card each or one bundle):

- nit: the new comment rests the argument on the seam ("refuses one that does not, at any holder count"). The seam keeps a named package unjudged when nothing holds the name, before the holders are sealed, and where the column is undeclared. The gate is still right there, by its own stale-column arm; the comment could say the gate does not depend on the seam.
- follow-up pins (probed green here, not in the suite): one outside holder with a non-holder named; a non-string column; a mixed batch.
- follow-up, owed with #31698 PR-2: one door-level pin on a real engine — an organization administrator names a holder, the row is stored with it, and the resolved access is that holder's set. Today's pins exercise the gate alone on a stand-in registry.
